data.long_meaning: The name Feeroz is derived from the Arabic root 'furz' which means 'to conquer' or 'to win'. This name signifies a victorious and courageous person, a lion among men. In Islamic history, there are many figures who bore this name, including the great Sufi saint, Sheikh Fariduddin Attar, who is known for his spiritual wisdom and teachings.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of courage and victory in the face of adversity.
data.etymology: Feeroz belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Victorious Lion.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Feeroz total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

historical_references.reference: Sultan Firuz Shah Tughlaq (1351-1388 AD) was a powerful ruler of the Tughlaq Empire based in Delhi, India. He is popularly known as Firuz Shah or Feroz Shah. During his reign, he undertook several major construction projects, including the famous complex of monuments in Mehrauli called Tughlakabad Fort and Adhai Din Ka Jhonpra.
historical_references.context: Sultan of Delhi, India, Construction projects

historical_references.reference: Sultan Firoz Shah Bahmani (1397-1422 AD) was the founder of the Bahmani Sultanate in Deccan, India. He is also known as Firuz Shah I and is considered one of the greatest Bahmani rulers. During his reign, he expanded the territory of the Bahmani Sultanate, which included parts of present-day Maharashtra, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, and Telangana. He is also known for his patronage of literature, art, and culture.
